Trace TP53 across the three portals: whi.answer:
## TP53 across the merged CRDC graph

**Gene node:** `TP53` (curie `hgnc:11998`) — the only entry whose `portal` list is `['gdc','pdc','gc']`, i.e. it's the single de-duplicated gene node visible from all three portals in the graph. (Related paralogs like `TP53BP1`/`TP53BP2`/`TP53TG3` etc. are separate nodes, mostly gdc/pdc only.)

Every mention of TP53 is carried on `biolink:related_to` edges from a `Study` or `Case` node into this gene node, and each edge records the source `file_id`, the `columns` it was extracted from, and the literal `raw_texts` matched — that's what lets us tell the role apart per portal.

### GDC (Genomic Data Commons) — role: somatic mutation/gene call on individual cases
- 10 distinct **Cases** reference TP53, all via the `gene_name` column (one case, TCGA-CZ-4864, also via a `peptide_target` column, raw text "P53"/"TP53").
- This is case-level mutation-calling data — TP53 shows up as an altered gene for a specific patient's tumor.
- Example cases: `DLBCL10932`, `C3N-02089`, `TCGA-CZ-4864`, and several `MP2PRT-*` submitter IDs (Wilms tumor cohort), each backed by 2–3 file IDs (e.g. `ncigdc:38d78186-75f0-41d8-be08-4923c989b8ae`, `ncigdc:ee5ca582-7eab-4a61-bc40-6cf4af390004`).

### PDC (Proteomic Data Commons) — role: identified protein/gene in proteogenomics studies (and a mutation-subtype flag in one)
- 27 distinct **Studies** reference TP53, almost all CPTAC cohorts (UCEC, GBM, AML, LSCC, LUAD, STAD, non-ccRCC) across Acetylome/Phosphoproteome/Glycoproteome/Metabolome data types.
- Dominant extraction column is `Gene` (27 studies, raw text "TP53", sometimes "tumor protein p53" or mouse ortholog "Trp53"), each backed by ~1–4 file IDs (e.g. `ncipdc:37d15522-8fd1-491e-9b57-decd4c162829` for the UCEC Confirmatory Acetylome study).
- In the **CPTAC STAD** studies specifically (Glycoproteome, Metabolome, Acetylome, Phosphoproteome — sharing file IDs like `ncipdc:57e3739e-fef2-4a53-a3a2-1f10eee9be27`), TP53 is *also* pulled from `Omic_gene`, `ACRG_subtype`, `V17`, `Genes`, and `Mutated_gene` columns — here the role shifts from "detected protein" to a **mutation-status/subtype annotation** for the study cohort.

### GC (General/Genomic Commons) — role: imaging antibody target, not sequence/protein-list data
- 1 **Study**: "Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN) imaging data" (`ncigc:phs002371_image`).
- Extracted from `Channel ID`, `Channel Name`, `Target Name`, `Antibody Name` columns, raw texts "p53", "Target:p53", "Channel:0:7 p53", "Cellular tumor antigen p53" — TP53/p53 here is the **antibody target of an imaging channel** (multiplex immunofluorescence), a fundamentally different kind of evidence than the mutation/proteomics roles above.
- 14 file IDs underlie this single study node (e.g. `ncigc:dg.4DFC/63398a90-53fb-5248-bdbc-638ad06a1288`).

### Summary
| Portal | Node type & count | Extraction column(s) | Inferred role |
|---|---|---|---|
| GDC | 10 Cases | `gene_name`, `peptide_target` | somatic mutation/gene call per patient |
| PDC | 27 Studies | `Gene` (+ `Omic_gene`,`ACRG_subtype`,`V17`,`Genes`,`Mutated_gene`,`Description` in STAD) | detected protein in proteogenomics assay; mutation/subtype flag in STAD |
| GC | 1 Study | `Channel ID/Name`, `Target Name`, `Antibody Name` | imaging antibody target (p53 protein) |

No case-level nodes carry TP53 in PDC or GC in this graph, and no study-level node carries it in GDC — the granularity of the mention (case vs. study) itself tracks each portal's native data model.

Which genes are called copy-number drive.answer:
## Answer

In this graph, "copy-number driver" annotations in PDC proteogenomic data come from a `CNV_Drivers` column found in supplementary tables attached to the **CPTAC STAD (Stomach Adenocarcinoma) proteogenomic study** — the only PDC study in the graph carrying this designation (checked across all `pdc`-portal gene edges for `cnv`/`copy`/`driver`/`cna`-related columns; nothing else surfaced).

The CNV-driver gene list is shared across all four STAD proteomic data tracks:
- CPTAC STAD Study – Acetylome (`pdc:c15b40f0-45c6-4789-8f47-f9513f3169bd`)
- CPTAC STAD Study – Phosphoproteome (`pdc:188bbdd1-6487-4c13-b149-692d75a655e3`)
- CPTAC STAD Study – Glycoproteome (`pdc:df29a1aa-a8a1-41ea-b153-bfdb57860023`)
- CPTAC STAD Study – Metabolome (`pdc:5ec67fd2-f161-494c-a350-dbe391943981`)
(file ids include `ncipdc:91f672ec-1de4-44b1-a624-47c819a33996`, `ncipdc:89c09f9c-9ba2-43e0-a3f9-ab1bdad3a47a`, `ncipdc:57e3739e-fef2-4a53-a3a2-1f10eee9be27`)

Of the 1,724 genes flagged as `CNV_Drivers` in this table, notable cancer-related genes that also carry a `gdc` tag on their node (i.e., are present in the Genomic Data Commons) include:
- **BRAF** — portals: gdc, pdc, gc
- **EGFR** — portals: gdc, pdc, gc
- **RB1** — portals: gdc, pdc, gc
- **SMAD4** — portals: gdc, pdc, gc
- **GATA6** — portals: gdc, pdc

All five come from the same CPTAC STAD study group listed above, since that's the only PDC study in the graph with copy-number-driver annotations.

**Caveat:** the graph doesn't distinguish these tables as a formal "CNV drivers" analysis output vs. a general gene-annotation table — it's inferred solely from the presence of a `CNV_Drivers` column whose cell values match gene symbols. If you want, I can pull the full 1,724-gene list or check whether GDC has copy-number-variant calls specifically for these STAD cases.

Which cancer genes appear in BOTH a Gene.answer:
## Answer

Yes — several well-known cancer genes co-occur in the shared metadata/text of a **GC** study's data files and a **PDC** proteomic study's data files. Intersecting the genes attached (via `biolink:related_to`, filtered on `portal` containing `gc` vs. `pdc`) to Study nodes across both portals yields (among others):

**TP53, KRAS, EGFR, BRCA2, PTEN, ATM, BRAF, CDKN2A, CTNNB1, ERBB2, MSH2, MYC, NRAS, RB1, SMAD4, VHL**

Example provenance:
- **GC side**: `PTEN`, `KRAS`, `BRCA2`, `EGFR` appear in the **caNanoLab Data** study (`ncigc:10.17917`); `EGFR`/`TP53` also appear in the **Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN) imaging data** study (`ncigc:phs002371_image`).
- **PDC side**: `PTEN` appears in numerous CPTAC proteomic studies, e.g. **CPTAC STAD Study – Phosphoproteome** (`pdc:188bbdd1-6487-4c13-b149-692d75a655e3`), **CPTAC GBM Discovery Study – CompRef Acetylome** (`pdc:b91a1590-f3a0-11ea-b1fd-0aad30af8a83`), and **CPTAC UCEC Confirmatory Study – CompRef Phosphoproteome** (`pdc:2f64929c-bab2-4d8c-a7e5-0164a9df7ec6`).

Note: these genes are linked to studies via file/metadata-derived `related_to` edges (columns/raw text mentions in the study's data files), not necessarily as curated "driver gene" annotations — but the same canonical `biolink:Gene` node is shared across both portals for each of these symbols.

Which genes have acetylation or glycosyl.answer:
This confirms a strong overlap. Here's a sample of genes found in PDC data with **both** acetylation/glycosylation site annotations and copy-number-driver annotations, all from the **CPTAC STAD Study** (Stomach Adenocarcinoma) proteogenomics dataset:

| Gene | Evidence columns | Source file/study |
|---|---|---|
| **ADAM10** | `Gene`, `Glycoprotein`, `Omic_gene`, `CNV_Drivers`, `Genes` | CPTAC STAD Study – Acetylome / Glycoproteome / Metabolome / Phosphoproteome |
| **ADAM17** | `Gene`, `Glycoprotein`, `CNV_Drivers`, `Genes` | CPTAC STAD Study – Acetylome / Glycoproteome |
| **ADAM9** | `Gene`, `Glycoprotein`, `CNV_Drivers`, `Genes` | CPTAC STAD Study – Acetylome / Glycoproteome |
| **ADGRE5** | `Gene`, `Glycoprotein`, `Omic_gene`, `CNV_Drivers`, `Genes` | CPTAC STAD Study – Acetylome / Glycoproteome / Metabolome |
| **PTK7** | `Gene`, `Glycoprotein`, `Omic_gene`, `CNV_Drivers`, `Genes` | CPTAC STAD Study – Acetylome / Glycoproteome / Metabolome / Phosphoproteome |
| **TOR1AIP2** | `Gene`, `Glycoprotein`, `Omic_gene`, `CNV_Drivers`, `Genes` | CPTAC STAD Study – Acetylome / Glycoproteome / Metabolome / Phosphoproteome |
| **SEL1L3** | `Gene`, `Glycoprotein`, `Omic_gene`, `CNV_Drivers`, `Genes` | CPTAC STAD Study – Acetylome / Glycoproteome / Metabolome / Phosphoproteome |

**How this was determined:**
- The knowledge graph stores, on each `Study → Gene` (`biolink:related_to`) edge, a `columns` list recording which source-table column names the gene was extracted from.
- "Acetylation/glycosylation site" evidence = columns like `Acetylsite`, `Mods`, or **`Glycoprotein`**.
- "Copy-number driver" evidence = the column **`CNV_Drivers`** (present in the same CPTAC STAD supplementary tables).
- All these genes come from the PDC portal (`portal` contains `'pdc'`), specifically the **CPTAC STAD Study** (multiple sub-datasets: Acetylome, Glycoproteome, Metabolome, Phosphoproteome — file IDs prefixed `ncipdc:`), where a single integrated results table annotates each gene with both a `Glycoprotein` flag and a `CNV_Drivers` flag in the same row.

Note: A broader `Acetylsite`-only search (e.g., in a different PDC acetylome file, `ncipdc:5823e9e8-...`) turned up mostly keratin genes (KRT5, KRT9, KRT14, etc.) and PON1, CDK8 — but those relationships didn't co-occur with a `CNV_Drivers` column, so they don't satisfy the "also a copy-number driver" criterion. The confirmed overlap is concentrated in the CPTAC STAD study's integrated tables.
